per_run.approach_summary: Profiled all 200 continuous features and found weak distributed signal, near-independent features, 10.2% positives, and no useful row-order effect. Four-fold CV compared regularized logistic regression, LightGBM, and extremely randomized trees over correlation-ranked subsets. Confirmation tests showed linear performance peaking near 125 features (AUC 0.8206), full-feature LightGBM reaching 0.8248, and complementary errors. A 30% linear / 70% LightGBM percentile-rank blend scored best at 0.8373 and was retrained on all research rows for transfer and real-test predictions.

Profiled all 200 anonymized features and tested standardized and rank-transformed logistic regression, L1 selection, ExtraTrees, LightGBM, and CatBoost with stratified out-of-fold AUC. Signals were numerous, weak, and nearly independent: regularized logistic and CatBoost were complementary. Confirmation calls mapped regularization and blend weights; scores included logistic C=0.02 at 0.8221, CatBoost at 0.8214, and the best 35% logistic / 65% CatBoost blend at 0.8368 (20 calls total). I attacked that result as a possible confirmation artifact using fresh five-fold OOF predictions, forward/backward contiguous holdouts, exact-overlap checks, and a research-vs-confirmation domain classifier. The same blend peaked in OOF testing at 0.8468, improved both temporal holdouts (0.8424 and 0.8508), had zero exact overlaps, and domain AUC was 0.4846, so the attack found no convincing confirmation-specific leakage or drift. The final models were retrained on all research rows and the identical blend was applied to transfer and real_test.

Profiled all 200 continuous features for missingness, uniqueness, marginal AUC, mutual information, correlations, row aggregates, and train/confirmation shift. The features were nearly independent and the signal was dense and additive: ridge logistic reached about 0.84 cross-validated AUC, tree ensembles about 0.79-0.82, RBF SVC about 0.85, Gaussian Naive Bayes about 0.862, and a strongly regularized per-feature cubic basis about 0.869. Repeated five-fold checks showed that clipping standardized values at +/-2.25 before forming linear, squared, and cubic terms stabilized tail effects and raised CV AUC to roughly 0.873-0.879 across split seeds. Confirmation feedback agreed: untrimmed cubic scored 0.8589, Gaussian NB 0.8556, RBF SVC 0.8380, and the best untrimmed blend 0.8603; the clipped cubic scored 0.8653, while Gaussian/kernel blends reduced it. The final model is therefore the single clipped cubic ridge-logistic model, refit on all 5,000 research rows.

Explored all 200 continuous features (5000 labeled rows; positive rate 0.1016), checking missingness, redundancy, marginal effects, feature correlations, and source shift. Stratified CV put heavily regularized logistic/LDA near 0.84 AUC, while random forests and boosting alone were roughly 0.77-0.81. Gaussian naive Bayes reached about 0.862 repeated-CV AUC, revealing that distributed class-specific location and scale changes across nearly all independent-looking features mattered more than generic tree interactions. Its confirmation AUC was 0.8559 versus 0.8306 for linear and 0.8158 for CatBoost. I attacked the best approach as a possible confirmation/ID artifact: forward validation was 0.8487, leave-contiguous-block-out AUC was 0.8612, target-versus-row_id AUC was 0.5103, and adversarial source classifiers could not separate research from confirmation, transfer, or sampled real-test rows (about 0.49-0.51). Allowing off-diagonal class covariance hurt CV, and independent half-samples retained correlated location/scale effects. The attack did find a genuine weakness: class-conditional marginals were platykurtic (median excess kurtosis near -0.5), so I revised Gaussian NB to independent symmetric exponential-power densities. Power 2.5 with 15% class-scale pooling scored about 0.8657 repeated CV and 0.8592 confirmation AUC. A small 15% rank blend with depth-4 CatBoost improved the exact same-fold OOF model and raised confirmation AUC to 0.8605; nearby shrinkage/blend settings were flat, while larger covariance and model weights were not. The final transfer and real-test predictions use that same all-research-trained power-NB/CatBoost rank blend.

DATA/STRUCTURE FINDINGS (what the exploration actually established)

Setup: 5000 labelled rows (10.16% positive), 200 continuous anonymised features, plus
1500 confirmation, 1500 transfer and 200000 real_test unlabelled rows. All four splits
are distributionally identical (per-feature means/sds and the ||z||^2 distribution match
to within sampling error), so nothing here is a covariate-shift problem.

1. The features are mutually independent. Over all 19900 pairs the maximum |Pearson r| is
   0.055 (about what the largest of 19900 null correlations should be at n=5000), and the
   correlation eigen-spectrum is flat (1.44 ... 0.64). There is no latent factor structure
   to exploit.

2. There are no interactions. I ran a score-test scan of all 20100 second-order terms
   (residual of a fitted linear-logit model vs. every centred product z_i*z_j). The 19900
   cross terms are exactly at the null (mean z^2 = 1.05, 56 with |z|>3 vs 53.7 expected),
   while the 200 self-squares are strongly enriched (mean z^2 = 2.38, 10 with |z|>3 vs 0.5
   expected). Confirmed downstream: depth-2 LightGBM (0.8375 CV) barely beats depth-1
   additive stumps and does not improve with more leaves, and a LightGBM fitted on the
   residual of my final score (init_score offset) adds exactly 0.0000 AUC.
   => the target is a purely ADDITIVE function of 200 independent features.

3. The additive per-feature response is exactly rank-2 in shape. Binning each feature into
   quantile bins and forming the 200 x B empirical log-density-ratio matrix, the SVD gives
   singular values 7.12, 4.78, 3.72, 3.48, 3.42, 3.26, ... i.e. two components above a flat
   noise floor. Component 1 is purely ANTISYMMETRIC and correlates -0.99 with the per-feature
   class mean shift; component 2 is purely SYMMETRIC and correlates -0.92 with the per-feature
   log class-variance ratio. Rank-3 and above is noise (rank-3 CV is worse). Cross-checked
   with orthonormal per-feature polynomials: signal/noise by degree is 5.6 (linear),
   2.1 (quadratic), 0.58, 0.43, 0.10, 0.37 -- the shared symmetric shape is not a clean
   parabola, it is flat across the middle ~90% of each feature and kicks up sharply only in
   the outer ~6% of each tail (see shapes below).

4. Consequently: log-odds = sum_k [ alpha_k * f1(u_k) + beta_k * f2(u_k) ], where u_k is the
   feature's marginal quantile, f1 is a monotone tail-weighted shape and f2 an "extremeness"
   shape. Fitted f1 over 32 quantile bins:
     +0.50 +0.30 +0.24 +0.18 +0.14 +0.12 +0.10 +0.09 +0.07 +0.08 +0.08 +0.07 +0.05 -0.00
     +0.00 +0.02 -0.01 -0.04 -0.03 -0.06 -0.06 -0.07 -0.07 -0.07 -0.11 -0.08 -0.11 -0.15
     -0.16 -0.22 -0.32 -0.50
   Fitted f2:
     +0.58 +0.25 +0.10 +0.00 -0.03 -0.03 -0.09 -0.08 -0.08 -0.07 -0.08 -0.09 -0.11 -0.10
     -0.05 -0.13 -0.08 -0.11 -0.11 -0.13 -0.08 -0.08 -0.08 -0.11 -0.04 -0.01 -0.01 -0.09
     -0.03 +0.10 +0.27 +0.58
   The two loading vectors are uncorrelated as signed quantities (r = 0.01) but
   corr(|alpha_k|, beta_k) = 0.74: the same features carry both effects. Practically, a value
   in either extreme tail of an *informative* feature raises the odds regardless of direction,
   on top of the directional effect. Aggregating that alone -- sum_k z_k^4 over all 200
   features -- is a single derived variable worth AUC 0.736 on its own, and ||z||^2 is
   worth 0.727, while the best single raw feature is only 0.583.

WHAT I TRIED (5-fold CV on research, averaged over 2-3 shuffle seeds)

  logistic regression, tuned C                              0.835
  LightGBM (depth 1 / depth 2 / 31 leaves)         0.829 / 0.838 / 0.838
  additive splines per feature (4/5/7 knots)                0.849-0.852
  logistic on [z, z^2] with tuned ridge                     0.855
  Gaussian naive Bayes (unequal variances)                  0.858
  block-penalised logistic [z | z^2 | global tail aggregates] 0.865
  shrunken centroids on orthonormal per-feature polys deg<=4 0.866
  shrunk-parameter Gaussian NB (mean & log-var-ratio shrinkage) 0.869
  binned rank-2 shared-shape model, labelled data only      0.852-0.859
  ---- semi-supervised EM using the 203k unlabelled rows ---- 0.889-0.891

THE THING THAT ACTUALLY WORKED: semi-supervised EM over the unlabelled pool.

Because the model class is "200 conditionally-independent features, two-component mixture",
the 203000 unlabelled rows (confirmation + transfer + real_test) carry real information about
the class-conditional per-feature densities. The bottleneck in the supervised fit is not the
shape functions (pooled across 200 features, they are well determined) but the 400 loadings,
estimated from only 508 positives. EM re-estimates them from ~200k softly-labelled rows.

Procedure (per B in {24,32,48,64} quantile bins, all bin edges from the 208k pooled rows):
  init  M = rank-2 truncation of the 200 x B labelled log-density-ratio table
  E     w_i = sigmoid(gamma * standardise(sum_k M[k, bin_k(x_i)]) + a), a solved so mean w = 0.1016
  M     re-accumulate weighted bin counts over unlabelled pool + hard-labelled research rows,
        re-form the log-ratio table, truncate to rank 2
  9 iterations; gamma = 1.5 (a CV-tuned score temperature; independently, Platt-scaling the
  raw log-ratio score gives slope 1.50, so the raw score is under-dispersed by exactly that
  factor -- the two numbers agreeing is a good sign the model is right)
Final score = mean of z-scored EM scores over the four bin resolutions + 0.25 * z-scored
supervised shrunken-centroid polynomial score (a small diversification, worth ~+0.001).

Diagnostics on the EM:
 - Rank-2 truncation is essential: unrestricted per-feature tables converge to 0.800,
   rank-3 to 0.877, rank-2 to 0.889.
 - Fixing the prior at the known base rate 0.1016 beats letting it float (it drifts to 0.40).
 - Fully UNSUPERVISED EM from random starts does NOT find the target (AUC 0.50 and 0.53
   against the held-out labels), so this is genuinely label-anchored refinement of a
   direction the labels supply, not unsupervised discovery of the class.
 - A leave-one-feature-out variant (re-estimating feature k's table from posteriors computed
   without feature k, which removes all self-reinforcement) jumps from 0.852 to 0.885 in a
   single iteration -- so the bulk of the gain is honest information transfer from the
   unlabelled rows, not self-confirmation. Its fixed point decays back to 0.869, exactly the
   supervised ceiling; the un-corrected version stabilises higher (0.889) because the extra
   self-consistency acts as a useful transductive/entropy-minimisation regulariser.
 - Held-out research rows used for CV are NOT in the unlabelled pool, so the 0.890 CV number
   is an honest out-of-pool estimate.

HOW FAR IS THIS FROM THE CEILING? Under the fitted model, p_i = sigmoid(score_i) on 40000
real_test rows implies a Bayes-optimal AUC of 0.887. My CV estimate is 0.890 and the
confirmation score is 0.878. Decile calibration on research is good (predicted vs actual:
0.002/0.004, 0.005/0.004, 0.008/0.010, 0.014/0.014, 0.022/0.006, 0.034/0.042, 0.053/0.052,
0.093/0.084, 0.194/0.222, 0.592/0.578). Combined with the null residual-LightGBM result,
I believe this is essentially at the irreducible limit for this generator.

CONFIRMATION SCORING LOOP (4 calls used of 20)
  1. EM blend over B in {32,48,64}, no gamma tuning       -> 0.8778
  2. supervised-only shrunken-centroid polynomial model   -> 0.8541
  3. final recipe (4 bin sizes, gamma=1.5, +0.25*sup)     -> 0.8782
  4. same, re-emitted with OOF-Platt-calibrated probs     -> 0.8782
Call 2 is the important one: it isolates the semi-supervised gain at +0.024 AUC on data the
model never saw labels for, matching the +0.026 seen in cross-validation. I deliberately
stopped there rather than tuning against a 1500-row proxy whose standard error (~0.015) is
larger than any remaining difference between my candidates.

FINAL MODEL: retrained on all 5000 labelled rows plus all 203000 unlabelled rows, applied to
transfer.json (in this file) and to all 200000 real_test.csv rows (final_predictions.csv).
Probabilities are Platt-calibrated on out-of-fold scores, so they are honest probabilities
rather than in-sample-sharpened ones.

DATA / STRUCTURE FOUND
200 continuous features, 5000 labelled rows (10.16% positive), 1500 confirmation, 1500 transfer,
200k real_test rows. I first mapped the geometry rather than fitting a model.

1. The 200 features are mutually independent: max |Pearson r| over all 19,900 pairs = 0.045, the
   correlation eigen-spectrum is flat (top eigenvalue 1.36 out of 200), and corr(z_j^2, z_k^2) ~ 0.
   Crucially they are also independent *within each class*: the off-diagonal within-class
   correlation sd is 0.0150 for the negatives (noise floor 0.0149, n=4492) and 0.0444 for the
   positives (noise floor 0.0444, n=508). So the Bayes-optimal rule is exactly additive,
   logit = c + sum_j LLR_j(x_j), and any interaction/tree machinery can only add variance.
   LightGBM confirmed this empirically (0.830 CV vs 0.826 for plain logistic regression).

2. Univariate signal is tiny (best single-feature AUC 0.583) but the mean shift is spread over
   essentially all 200 features: the per-feature t-statistics have sd 2.58 (null 1.0) with excess
   kurtosis -0.75, i.e. the effects are dense and roughly uniformly distributed, not sparse.
   No feature selection is appropriate; the top feature carries only 1.5% of the effect mass.

3. THE MAIN FINDING - a global dispersion effect that no univariate view and no tree can see.
   Positives are not only shifted, they are *wider* in nearly every feature: sd1/sd0 has mean
   1.031 (per-half se 0.0036, ~8 sigma) and is >1 for 76.5% of features. The purely
   label-free statistic sum_j z_j^2 (features standardised with real_test moments; zero fitted
   parameters) already scores AUC 0.727 on research and 0.7385 on the held-out confirmation rows.
   GaussianNB, which is the only common off-the-shelf model that uses per-class variances, jumps
   to 0.858 while logistic regression / LDA / LightGBM all sit at 0.826-0.836.

4. The variance inflation decomposes cleanly: rho_j - 1 = 0.0185 + 1.00 * d_j^2, where d_j is the
   class mean shift in sd units. A constant global part plus a part proportional to the squared
   mean shift. I validated this on independent halves of the research rows (d estimated on half A,
   rho on half B: corr 0.262 +- 0.006 vs a permuted null of 0.004).

5. Marginals are symmetric and strongly platykurtic (pooled excess kurtosis -0.50, per-feature
   -0.83..-0.08) with bounded support around +-3 sd. That matters twice: the Gaussian LLR is
   misspecified, and the sample mean is not the efficient estimator of a location shift for a
   short-tailed density.

MODEL
A shared-shape naive Bayes. Because conditional independence is exact but only ~508 positives are
available to estimate 200 densities, all the leverage comes from sharing shape across features:

    logit(x_i) = c + sum_j [ A(z_ij) + d_j * B(z_ij) + d_j^2 * C(z_ij) ]

z is standardised with real_test's 200k-row moments; A, B, C are cubic-spline functions estimated
from all 200*5000 (feature,row) observations at once, so they are extremely well determined
(the design collapses to 30 columns on 5000 rows). Only d_j is per-feature. A(z) comes out
symmetric and U-shaped (the global dispersion), B(z) antisymmetric and monotone (the shift),
C(z) the d^2-linked dispersion. This is a strict generalisation of GaussianNB, which is the
special case A,B,C = quadratic polynomials.

Two refinements that paid off:
 - d_j estimated from sign(z)|z|^1.7 rather than the mean, normalised by E[g'(z)] on real_test.
   Chosen by split-half reliability (correlation of d estimated on disjoint halves rose from
   0.733 to 0.747, ~7% less estimator noise), *not* by CV AUC. Gave +0.0027 CV.
 - Uniform-prior empirical-Bayes shrinkage of d_j, and a 4-basis ensemble (three knot sets +
   Hermite polynomials) for stability.

Things I tried that did NOT help, and why: rank-Gauss transforming the features (-0.002; it
compresses exactly the tails where A(z) lives); replacing the plug-in d_j with a jointly
ridge-fitted 200-coefficient GAM (converges to the plug-in as the penalty grows, never beats it -
evidence the plug-in is already efficient); using the density-derived location score
psi = -dlogf/dz from the 200k unlabelled rows (theoretically 17% more efficient, but the density
hits its bounded support so psi explodes at the edges - split-half reliability *fell* to 0.676);
a free per-feature term for the variance-ratio residual; blending in LightGBM (+0.0004, noise).
Semi-supervised use of the 200k unlabelled rows is provably near-worthless here: with prevalence
known, the unlabelled means pin down (1-pi)mu0 + pi*mu1, which the labelled data already gives -
the full-information MLE has exactly the same se(d) = 0.0468 as the labelled-only estimate.

SCORES
5x5 repeated-CV on research, final pipeline: 0.8782 +- 0.0012.
Confirmation calls (4 used, none used to select anything): plain L2 logistic 0.8274;
label-free dispersion statistic sum z^2 0.7385; an earlier single-basis version 0.8665;
final model 0.8712.

ATTACKING MY OWN RESULT
I tried to break the claim that the confirmation score reflects a real, transferable pattern.
 a) Fold artifact / CV-tuning artifact. Refuted the hardest way available: the strongest single
    structural claim (dispersion) is carried by sum_j z_j^2, which has NO fitted parameters at all
    and standardises using only unlabelled real_test rows. It scores 0.727 on research and 0.7385
    on confirmation. A fold artifact cannot survive that. Separately, the margin of the full model
    over plain logistic regression is +0.044 in CV and +0.044 on confirmation - the gain
    replicates exactly out of sample rather than shrinking.
 b) Confirmation overfitting. I made only 4 scorer calls and no hyperparameter, basis, transform
    or shrinkage choice was ever made using a confirmation score; every selection came from 5x5
    repeated CV or from split-half reliability of the effect estimates. The confirmation number is
    therefore an honest holdout, and it sits 0.007 below CV for both the baseline and the final
    model - a uniform sampling offset, not a model-specific collapse.
 c) Coincidental overlap with research rows. No exact duplicates. 1-NN distance from confirmation
    to research (min 14.88, median 16.91) is indistinguishable from research-to-research
    (min 15.13, median 16.91) and real_test-to-research (min 14.79, median 16.92). In 200
    independent dimensions nothing is anyone's neighbour; memorisation is impossible, and the
    model has only 30 free coefficients besides the 200 d_j anyway.
 d) A spurious dominant feature. The effect mass is dense: top feature 1.5%, top 10 features
    13.9%, top 50 features 56.7%. Removing any one feature is irrelevant.
 e) The d^2 dispersion term being noise-fitting. Validated across disjoint halves (see 4 above).
 f) Distribution shift to real_test - the one that would actually invalidate the transfer.
    An initial float32 pass appeared to show feature x_165 shifted by 0.71 sd; that turned out to
    be catastrophic cancellation in float32 accumulation on a near-constant column (mean 5.0189,
    sd 0.0072), not a real shift. Recomputed in float64, the largest standardised mean difference
    between research and real_test is 0.052 against a sampling se of 0.014, and the sd ratios lie
    in [0.973, 1.020]. A LightGBM two-sample discriminator between real_test and each of
    research / confirmation / transfer scores 0.512 / 0.508 / 0.515 - chance. No shift.
 g) Residual structure the model misses. Per-feature 8-bin score tests on the OOF residuals give
    total chi2 = 1407 against a null of 1600, with zero features at p<0.01 (2 expected).
    Class-conditional skewness differences show no excess over noise (sd 0.088 vs noise 0.109).
    The location-scale + shared-shape form has absorbed the per-feature signal.
The attack did not turn up anything that would make me revise the approach, so it is unchanged.

WHAT LIMITS THE SCORE
This is estimation-limited, not structure-limited. The OOF calibration curve is a smooth sigmoid
(top 5% of scores are 68% positive), so the labels are genuinely stochastic. With d_j known
exactly the linear component's class separation would rise from 1.462 to 1.584 sd, implying a
ceiling near AUC 0.89; the whole remaining gap is noise in 200 effect estimates read off 508
positives, and no amount of extra unlabelled data or model capacity can close it.

The identical fitted pipeline (retrained on all 5000 research rows) produced both the transfer
predictions below and final_predictions.csv; probabilities are out-of-fold calibrated
(mean predicted rate 0.1007 on real_test vs 0.1016 observed prevalence).
